subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Should Microsoft Teams uploads standardize on a five-minute base deadline plus transfer budget at 256 KiB/s, and should this PR or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104288 land first as the shared-helper owner?
rationale: The tests and HTTPS proof establish that the mechanism works, but the repository does not establish the proposed throughput floor or cross-PR ownership order as an existing production contract.

options.title: Approve and land this first
options.body: Accept the proposed transfer policy, land this focused consent-upload change as the helper owner, then rebase the broader SharePoint-send PR onto it.

options.title: Land the broader PR first
options.body: Let the SharePoint-send PR own the shared helper and policy, then reduce this branch to the consent-path integration and tests.

options.title: Revise the transfer policy
options.body: Choose a different throughput floor or timeout cap from Microsoft service expectations before either PR lands.

recommendation.title: Approve and land this first
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed transfer policy, land this focused consent-upload change as the helper owner, then rebase the broader SharePoint-send PR onto it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent work on the same Microsoft Teams file-consent network and SSRF boundary.
